original_question: Let (u_i)_{i >= 1} be a strictly increasing sequence of integers greater than 1 and let (v_i)_{i >= 1} satisfy v_i < u_i. Construct the more general sieve that, at step i, keeps the v_i-th number among the next u_i - 1 remaining numbers and deletes every u_i-th remaining number. What relationship between the generators (u_i), (v_i), and the resulting remaining sequence can be proved?
target_in_paper: Entry 32, "More General-Sequence Sieve": the open problem asking to study the relationship between the sequences u_i, v_i and the remaining sequence produced by the sieve. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it uses a strictly increasing sequence (u_i) with u_i > 1, introduces a second sequence (v_i) selecting which survivor to keep at step i, defines the iterative sieve by keeping a chosen element among the next u_i-1 surviving numbers and deleting every u_i-th remaining number, and asks for the relationship between the generators and the resulting remaining sequence. This is exactly the scope of Entry 32 and does not broaden the problem beyond the paper. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient set should be stated explicitly: the construction starts from the natural numbers set, i.e. {1,2,3,...}, not an arbitrary integer set. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The sequence (v_i) is not just required to satisfy v_i < u_i; it is another positive integer sequence, so the intended condition is 1 <= v_i < u_i for every i. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The first step is slightly special in wording: one keeps the v_1-th number among 1,2,3,...,u_1-1, whereas for later steps one keeps the v_i-th number among the next u_i-1 remaining numbers. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The paper explicitly names u_i and v_i the sieve generators; that terminology is part of the official formulation. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The paper presents this as an open-ended problem to "study the relationship" between the generators and the surviving sequence, not as a theorem with a predetermined type of conclusion. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

No extra algebraic data are involved here: there is no ambient ring, field, operator, degree condition, homogeneity, or nilpotency hypothesis—only a sieve on the natural numbers. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
refined_question: Let (u_i)_{i>=1} be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with u_i > 1, and let (v_i)_{i>=1} be a positive integer sequence with 1 <= v_i < u_i for all i. Starting from the natural numbers set N = {1,2,3,...}, define the more general sieve recursively as follows: at step 1, keep the v_1-th number among 1,2,3,...,u_1-1 and delete every u_1-th number; for each step i >= 2, keep the v_i-th number among the next u_i-1 numbers that remain after the previous steps and delete every u_i-th remaining number. With u_i and v_i regarded as sieve generators, study the relationship between the generator sequences (u_i), (v_i) and the remaining sequence produced by this more general sieve. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Entry 32 almost verbatim. The nearby context matters: Entry 30 first introduces the consecutive sieve and remarks that, instead of always keeping the first surviving number, one could keep any member of the surviving k-plet; Entry 31 then abstracts this by using a strictly increasing generator sequence (u_i); Entry 32 sharpens that abstraction by specifying the kept position through a second positive integer sequence (v_i). Therefore the paper-faithful refinement should remain an open problem about a sieve on N determined by two sieve generators, and should not add goals such as density, primality, asymptotics, or classification that the paper does not state here. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
